mappings.note: The Sea of Tranquility being on the Moon identifies a feature of a celestial object. Not LO-11, because the item asks where it is, not who landed there.

A cosmic year is an astronomical unit of time, a measurement matter, and the frame's only measurement outcome, LO-7, covers angles only. Cited at competency level for the same reason as the light-year items.
Venus being hotter than Mercury despite being farther out is a phenomenon explained by its atmosphere, exactly the relate-to-cause outcome. Not LO-2, because the planets are not being classified.
The nucleus of a comet is a structural part of a celestial object. Not LO-4, because nothing is explained causally.
The fastest planet ranks solar-system bodies by a property. Not LO-5, because orbital motion is not being explained.
The planet nearest the Sun orders the solar system's members. Shares the outcome with its neighbours because the frame offers one astronomy code.
The largest planet ranks celestial objects by size. Not LO-1, whose examples are terrestrial materials and organisms.
The brightest planet characterises a celestial object by appearance. Not LO-4, since the brightness is not explained.
Naming the chief air pollutant is knowledge of an environmental hazard, which LO-13 covers. Not LO-4, reserved here for items that tie a pollutant to a specific effect.
Sorting gases into greenhouse and non-greenhouse is classification of materials by a property. Not LO-4, used here for the mechanism by which those gases warm the planet.
The launch of the Ganga Action Plan is an organised effort to protect the environment. Not LO-4, because no pollution effect is being traced.
Carbon dioxide absorbing infrared radiation is the mechanism behind warming, a phenomenon and its cause. Not LO-2, because no gas is being classified here.
The pollutant element in vehicle exhaust is knowledge of an environmental hazard. Not LO-4, because no effect of that element is named in the stem.
Marble cancer caused by acid rain is the deterioration of monuments LO-4 names word for word. Not LO-13, because the item explains rather than proposes a remedy.
Particulate matter defined as dispersed solids and liquids is hazard terminology. Not LO-2, because the item defines a pollutant rather than sorting materials.
The pollution damaging the Taj Mahal is the monument-deterioration example in LO-4. Not LO-13, since no protective measure is proposed.
The major causes of air pollution relate a phenomenon to its sources. Not LO-13, because nothing is done about them in the item.
The Bhopal tragedy traced to a gas leak relates a disaster to its cause. Not LO-13, since no coping measure is asked for.
Which contaminant harms aquatic life most links a pollutant to its effect. Not LO-13, because the item identifies the harm rather than the remedy.
Removing dissolved salt to make water usable is purifying water, named verbatim in LO-12. Not LO-13, which covers protecting the source rather than treating the water.
Picking the non-biodegradable pollutant is the biodegradable/non-biodegradable segregation LO-12 names. Not LO-2, because the point is what to do with the waste.
The major source of water pollution relates the problem to its cause. Not LO-12, since no purification follows.
Choosing the irrigation method that saves water is using a resource judiciously, LO-13 word for word. Not LO-12, because the point is conservation rather than a farming practice.
Carbon monoxide from exhaust causing harm links a pollutant to its effect. Not LO-13, because no protective step is proposed.
Smog as smoke plus fog is the smog-formation example named verbatim in LO-4. Not LO-2, since gases are not being classified.
CFCs from refrigeration damaging ozone links a substance to an environmental effect. Deliberately different from the item asking merely where CFCs are used, which is an application.
What acid rain contains underpins the monument-damage causal chain in LO-4. Not LO-6, because no reaction equation is written.
Marble cancer caused by acid rain is a duplicate of the earlier item and takes the same causal outcome. Not LO-13, since no remedy is offered.
Defining the greenhouse effect states the mechanism that causes warming. Not LO-2, which is used for sorting the gases themselves.
Listing which gases count as greenhouse gases is classification of materials by a property. Not LO-4, used for the warming mechanism itself.
Chlorination as the usual chemical purification is purifying water, LO-12's own example. Not LO-13, because the water is treated rather than the environment protected.
The Ganga Action Plan being a river-cleaning programme is an effort to protect the environment. Not LO-12, because it is a public programme, not a household practice.
Van Mahotsav as a tree-planting drive is an organised environmental effort. Grouped with the Ganga Action Plan items for the same reason.
The major source of water pollution relates the problem to its cause. Duplicate of an earlier item and coded the same way.
What is damaging the Taj Mahal is the monument-deterioration example in LO-4. Duplicate in substance of the earlier Taj Mahal item.
Identifying a greenhouse gas sorts gases by a property. Grouped with the other greenhouse-gas classification items rather than with the mechanism items on LO-4.
What water pollution is due to relates the phenomenon to its causes. Not LO-12, because no purification is carried out.
The proportion of nitrogen in air is the composition of a material, which LO-1 covers through properties and structure. Not LO-13, because no hazard or protective action is involved.
Where CFCs are used, in refrigerators and air conditioners, is an everyday application of a material. Kept apart from the ozone-damage item, which is causal and sits on LO-4.
